name: Elon Musk

summary.text: Elon Musk runs Tesla and SpaceX and bought Twitter (now X) for $44 billion in October 2022. He co-founded the brain-implant company Neuralink and was a co-founder of OpenAI in 2015, which he sued in 2024. A jury and judge rejected that suit on statute-of-limitations grounds in May 2026. In 1999 he founded X.com, which merged with Confinity in 2000 to form what became PayPal.

facts.claim: Ashlee Vance's biography of Elon Musk, as cited by InsideHook, says his father Errol Musk ran an engineering business that handled large projects such as office buildings, retail complexes, residential subdivisions and an air force base.

sources.title: Everything to Know About Errol Musk, Elon Musk's "Brilliant," "Terrible" Father

facts.claim: Errol Musk told Business Insider South Africa in 2018 that he became a half-owner of an emerald mine in Zambia in the 1980s. InsideHook notes that little corroborates his account, and no registration, contract or ownership record has been published. Walter Isaacson's 2023 biography gives a different account: Errol sold a light plane in 1986 to a businessman in exchange for emeralds from a Zambian mine that businessman owned, which was never registered. Isaacson quotes Errol saying none of it was legal. Business Insider wrote that this supports Elon Musk's statement that his father never owned an emerald mine.

sources.title: Everything to Know About Errol Musk, Elon Musk's "Brilliant," "Terrible" Father
Elon Musk really was telling the truth by saying his father Errol never owned an emerald mine, biographer says

facts.claim: Elon Musk's statements on the emeralds have changed. In a 2014 AskMen interview he said his father had a share in an emerald mine in Zambia. In a December 2019 tweet he wrote that his father didn't own an emerald mine and that he worked his way through college, ending up with about $100,000 in student debt.

sources.title: Elon Musk really was telling the truth by saying his father Errol never owned an emerald mine, biographer says

facts.claim: Ashlee Vance's biography says Errol Musk gave the brothers $28,000 while they were starting Zip2. Elon Musk told Rolling Stone in 2017 that this was not true and that the first funding came from angel investors. He then tweeted in December 2019 that his father provided 10% of a roughly $200,000 angel round 'much later'.

sources.title: Who Is Elon Musk's Dad, Errol Musk? (by Gabrielle Bienasz)

facts.claim: Queen's University's alumni magazine says Musk spent his freshman and sophomore years at Queen's in Kingston, Ontario, from 1989 to 1991, then transferred to the University of Pennsylvania. According to the Washington Post, he holds Canadian citizenship through his mother.

sources.title: Rocket man

sources.publisher: The Washington Post (via Anchorage Daily News)
sources.title: Elon Musk, enemy of 'open borders,' launched his career working illegally

facts.claim: At about 19, while at Queen's, Musk was the sole intern on a small internal consulting team at the Bank of Nova Scotia led by executive Peter Nicholson. He proposed buying discounted Latin American debt in expectation of Brady bond conversions, and the bank's leadership declined. This is the only documented pre-1999 tie to a financial institution found.

sources.title: The little-known story about Elon Musk's first post-grad internship (excerpt from Jimmy Soni, The Founders)

facts.claim: Musk received a dual degree in economics and physics from Penn's College and Wharton School in 1997. PayPal's 2001 S-1 lists his Penn physics degree and Wharton economics degree. Stanford says he was admitted to a graduate program in materials science and engineering in 1995 but has no record of him enrolling.

facts.claim: The Washington Post reported that Mohr Davidow Ventures invested $3 million in Zip2 in 1996, and that the funding agreement gave the Musk brothers and an associate 45 days to obtain legal work status or the firm could reclaim its investment. The Post cited a 2005 Musk email saying he had 'no legal right to stay in the country' when he started Zip2. A Zip2 board member and a former HR staffer recalled work authorizations arriving around 1997. Musk did not respond to the Post. In a 2020 podcast he said he was 'legally there' but 'meant to be doing student work'. After the story ran, he posted on X that he was 'in fact allowed to work' and had been on a J-1 visa that transitioned to an H-1B.

facts.claim: Compaq completed its acquisition of Zip2 Corporation in April 1999 for total consideration of about $307 million in cash, plus employee stock options and acquisition costs. Zip2 was folded into Compaq's AltaVista business. Secondary sources date the announcement to February 1999.

sources.title: Business career of Elon Musk

facts.claim: X.com was incorporated in March 1999 to provide internet banking. It sold Musk 5,400,000 common shares at $0.0033 per share in March 1999 and 600,000 at $0.033 in May 1999. Musk was CEO of X.com from March to December 1999. Gale's encyclopedia says about $25 million in venture capital came from Musk, Bill Harris and Sequoia Capital.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form S-1 registration statement
X.Com

facts.claim: In November 1999, X.com agreed to buy First Western National Bank from Community Bankshares, Inc. (CBI), subject to regulatory approval, and to solicit customers for First Western accounts. In December 2000 it discontinued internet banking and ended the purchase agreement, paying CBI a $1.0 million termination fee plus $1.0 million in reimbursed losses. The 2001 S-1 warned that states could find PayPal was engaged in unauthorized banking.
facts.quote: we agreed to purchase CBI's wholly owned subsidiary, First Western National Bank

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form S-1 registration statement

facts.claim: After X.com launched in December 1999, the company conceded that its system had made it too easy to move money out of other people's accounts. Suspicious transfers were detected and reversed. No regulatory action over the episode was found.

sources.title: X.Com

facts.claim: X.com merged with Confinity on March 30, 2000, with X.com as the surviving company. Musk was CEO of the combined company from May to September 2000. Isaacson's and Vance's biographies say the board removed him in September 2000 while he was away on a delayed honeymoon and installed Peter Thiel as CEO.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form S-1 registration statement

facts.claim: In July 2000, PayPal assigned Musk its right to repurchase 3,149,055 Series B shares from former CEO Bill Harris. Musk gave the company a note for about $389,000 at 6.6% interest, and the note and interest were forgiven after the February 2002 IPO. Under a May 2001 separation agreement, PayPal bought back common and preferred shares from Musk for about $762,666.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form S-1 registration statement
PayPal, Inc. prospectus (Form 424B1), 6,000,000 shares

facts.claim: As of May 31, 2002, Musk beneficially owned 7,109,989 PayPal shares (11.7%). He sold 600,000 shares as a selling stockholder in PayPal's June 2002 offering at $19.00 per share, leaving 6,509,989 shares (10.7%). The eBay merger agreement was signed on July 7, 2002.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. prospectus (Form 424B1), 6,000,000 shares
eBay Inc. Form S-4 (PayPal merger)

facts.claim: Musk was one of the PayPal insiders and investors, together holding about 28.1% of PayPal's stock, who signed a July 7, 2002 agreement to vote for the eBay merger. eBay completed the purchase on October 3, 2002, in a stock deal valued at about $1.5 billion at 0.39 eBay shares per PayPal share. Musk's proceeds are reported at about $176 million, a figure that comes from Vance's biography rather than a filing.

sources.title: eBay Inc. Form S-4 (PayPal merger)

facts.claim: On September 26, 2025, Democrats on the House Oversight Committee released daily calendars obtained from Epstein's estate under subpoena. One entry dated December 6, 2014 reads: 'Reminder: Elon Musk to island December 6 (is this still happening?).' NBC News noted the document gives no information about how the entry came about or whether the anticipated visit ever occurred.
facts.quote: One calendar entry dated December 6, 2014, reads: "Reminder: Elon Musk to island December 6 (is this still happening?)." ... The document gives no information about how the entry came about, what level of planning was involved or whether the anticipated visit ever occurred.

sources.title: Oversight Democrats Release Third Batch of Documents from Jeffrey Epstein Estate, Includes Elon Musk, Peter Thiel, Steve Bannon, Prince Andrew Mentions
Epstein calendar released by Democrats mentions Elon Musk, who denies visiting his island

facts.claim: Responding on X to a post about the September 2025 calendar release, Musk wrote 'This is false' without elaborating. NBC News reported that Musk has said he declined repeated invitations to visit Epstein's island and has never visited it.
facts.quote: He wrote "This is false" without elaborating. ... Musk has said that he declined repeated invitations to visit the island owned by the convicted sex offender.

sources.title: Epstein calendar released by Democrats mentions Elon Musk, who denies visiting his island

facts.claim: The Justice Department's Epstein file release in January 2026 included emails between Musk and Epstein from 2012 and 2013; Time counted 16. CBS News reported that in a November 25, 2012 email Epstein asked Musk how many people he would bring for the helicopter ride to the island, that Musk replied the group would be small and asked about party plans on the island, and that in a 2013 email Epstein asked whether Musk would come to the Caribbean for Christmas.
facts.quote: in a Nov. 25, 2012 email, Epstein asked Musk how many people he would be bringing for the helicopter ride to the island. Musk replied that the group would be small, and he also asked about the party plans on the island. In a later 2013 email, Epstein asked Musk if he would come to the Caribbean for Christmas.

sources.title: Bill Gates, Elon Musk among big names in Epstein files. Here's what the latest documents show.
Elon Musk's Emails to Jeffrey Epstein Revealed in Latest File Release

facts.claim: After the January 2026 release, Musk posted on X that he had 'very little correspondence' with Epstein and did not go to his island, that he 'declined repeated invitations to go to his island or fly on his Lolita Express,' and that he was aware some emails 'could be misinterpreted and used by detractors to smear my name.' He called the release 'a distraction' and wrote, 'No one pushed harder than me to have the Epstein files released.'
facts.quote: he wrote that he declined repeated invitations to go to his island or fly on his 'Lolita Express', and that he was aware some emails could be misinterpreted and used by detractors to smear my name. He called the release "a distraction" and said "No one pushed harder than me to have the Epstein files released."

openQuestions: Exact dollar proceeds to Musk from the eBay deal: ~$176M (Vance via Wikipedia) not verified against a filing. SEC numbers imply ~2.54M eBay shares for his 6,509,989 post-offering PayPal shares, plus ~$11.4M gross from 600,000 shares sold at $19 in June 2002; eBay share price at close not checked.
Original Feb 1999 Compaq/Zip2 announcement coverage (NYT, CNET, Feb 16-17, 1999) could not be opened; Wikipedia gives $305M in one place, SEC filings give ~$307M cash.
Mohr Davidow's 1996 investment terms (majority ownership claim from Britannica) could not be opened (403).
Musk's 2023 X posts denying the emerald mine and the million-Dogecoin offer (News24/Fin24, Daily Investor) could not be opened; 2018 Business Insider South Africa originals not located.

Date of arrival in Canada: Queen's Alumni Review says both 'came in 1990' and 'from 1989 to 1991' at Queen's; Wikipedia says June 1989 arrival. Birth date/place (28 June 1971, Pretoria) not opened in a source this session.
X.com December 1999-January 2000 unauthorized ACH transfers (CNN/Computerworld Feb 2000, ~$10,000 reported) could not be opened (HTTP 451).
Sequoia's direct investment amount in X.com's 1999 Series A (beyond the $5M secondary purchase from Musk) not confirmed from a filing.
Musk's 1994-95 internships (Pinnacle Research Institute, Rocket Science Games) not researched for any government or defense ties; no record found of any government or intelligence tie before 1999.
The CBS and Time articles on the 2012-13 Musk emails are undated in the search results; confirm publication dates and the DOJ release date (reported as January 30, 2026).
